questions.q: Which chapter's lesson did execute_containment()'s approval-gate requirement in Lesson 29 directly implement as code?
options: Chapter 3's Lesson 12, on containment actions and the approval gate they need
Chapter 1 (Python fundamentals)
Chapter 6 (DevSecOps fundamentals)
Chapter 7 (securing the pipeline itself)
questions.explain: Lesson 12's principle -- containment actions need an approval gate -- is exactly what the approved_by parameter enforces in actual code in Lesson 29.

questions.q: Why does the review say Chapter 5's lessons on ChatOps and idempotency matter to the Lesson 29 pipeline?
options: They are unrelated; Chapter 5 only applies to ticketing systems
The pipeline posts proposed actions to an approval channel and tracks processed incident IDs so re-running it never double-contains the same finding
Chapter 5 is where Microsoft Graph authentication was first introduced
They explain why dry_run defaults to True
questions.explain: Posting to an approval channel is the ChatOps pattern, and tracking processed IDs is the idempotency pattern -- both from Chapter 5, applied to a live pipeline instead of a standalone example.

questions.q: What specific Chapter 6 lesson is security_gate.py's Critical/High-only threshold a direct application of?
options: Lesson 21, on shifting left
Lesson 22, on SAST and dependency scanning tools
Lesson 24, on setting security gates that fail a build without slowing every build
Lesson 20, on error handling and idempotency
questions.explain: Lesson 24 argued that a gate blocking on every finding trains developers to ignore it -- the Critical/High-only threshold in security_gate.py is that argument enforced in code.

questions.q: According to this review, what is the real relationship between Lesson 29's gated script and Lesson 31's Caldera Finance case study?
options: They are unrelated topics covered back-to-back by coincidence
Lesson 31 proves that automation should never be used for containment
Lesson 31 describes a bug in the exact script built in Lesson 29
Lesson 31 is the same material as Lessons 29-30, viewed from what happens when the guardrails are skipped
questions.explain: Caldera's script lacked the dry-run default and approval gate that Bramwell's script had -- the case study shows the cost of skipping guardrails this chapter built, not a flaw in Bramwell's own pipeline.

questions.q: What course comes next in the Advanced Specialization stage after this course, according to the review?
options: Digital Forensics and Malware Analysis
Azure & AWS Cloud Security
Zero Trust & Enterprise Security Capstone
Ethical Hacking, Penetration Testing & Purple Team
questions.explain: Zero Trust & Enterprise Security Capstone is the final course of the Advanced Specialization stage, closing it out before Expert Specialization begins.
